narrativeReportMd:
# Parameters R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`Parameters` keeps the same identity and overall content model, but one local `value[x]` choice type was removed and six R6-only choice types were added. The hard R4-to-R6 break is that an R4 `Parameters.parameter.valueContributor` can validate in R4 but is not an allowed R6 choice. The main reverse-direction risk is that R6 Parameters can use new value choices such as `valueCodeableReference` or `valueInteger64` that R4 cannot represent without an operation-specific transform.

## Scope
The analysis covers the local `Parameters` resource definition and its `parameter` backbone. Inherited changes from `Resource`, `Element`, `BackboneElement`, and extension infrastructure are excluded and should be handled by those base-artifact reports.

## Main migration themes
The important migration work is around operation parameter payloads and generated choice accessors. Systems that treat `value[x]` as a fixed enum of choice names need to remove or map `Contributor` when moving forward to R6, and they need a policy for R6-only datatypes when exporting back to R4. Two semantic text changes also matter for interoperability review: R6 no longer carries the R4 comment that only one level of nested `part` is allowed, and R6 text explicitly mentions additional resources under `parameter.resource`.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact local finding is `Parameters:TYPE_DOMAIN:Parameters.parameter.value[x]:f0cf76`, the removal of `Contributor` from `value[x]`. `Parameters:TYPE_DOMAIN:Parameters.parameter.value[x]:6ae434` is high impact for R6-to-R4 conversion because six R6 choices have no R4 counterpart.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most useful for the semantic text changes: whether a trading partner enforces the old one-level `part` comment, and whether an R6 operation will actually use additional resources in `parameter.resource`. The supplied computable definitions are clear, but the official narrative rationale and operation examples would improve confidence.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The type-domain changes could have been made less disruptive by retaining deprecated aliases or by defining cross-version extensions, but that would preserve obsolete or R6-specific model surface in the base resource. The R6 design appears to favor a current datatype set and relies on conversion tooling or operation-specific rules for cross-version exchange.

## Follow-up analysis
Review the base `Resource` report for inherited language/id/implicitRules behavior and the datatype reports for `Contributor`, `integer64`, `CodeableReference`, `RatioRange`, `Availability`, `ExtendedContactDetail`, and `VirtualServiceDetail`.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 `Parameters` is the same resource identity as R4, but its local `value[x]` type set changed: `Contributor` was removed, while six R6-only datatypes were added. The clearest hard break is old-valid `valueContributor` content becoming invalid in R6; the biggest reverse-direction concern is R6 `valueCodeableReference`, `valueInteger64`, and related choices not fitting R4. Confidence is high for the computable type changes and medium for lower-impact semantic text changes because official narrative rationale was not available.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should focus on generated choice-type APIs, validators, serializers, and operation-specific transforms. R4-to-R6 conversion needs a policy for `valueContributor` because no generic lossless R6 `Parameters` value choice replaces it. R6-to-R4 conversion needs per-parameter rules for `integer64`, `CodeableReference`, `RatioRange`, `Availability`, `ExtendedContactDetail`, and `VirtualServiceDetail`, plus review of any deeply nested `part` structures or additional-resource payloads.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for artifact identity, cardinalities, local element presence, constraints, flags, and `value[x]` type-domain changes because they are directly visible in both StructureDefinitions and the R6 XML schema. Confidence is medium for semantic findings based on comments/definitions because the package lacks official diff notes and full rendered narrative pages that could clarify intended conformance impact.

findings.title: Parameters.parameter.value[x] no longer accepts Contributor

oldState.summary: R4 `Parameters.parameter.value[x]` allowed `Contributor` as one of 50 datatype choices.
oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, an operation parameter could carry contributor metadata using the JSON/XML choice name `valueContributor`.

newState.summary: R6 `Parameters.parameter.value[x]` no longer includes `Contributor`; the R6 core package also has no `StructureDefinition-Contributor.json`.
newState.narrativeMd: In R6, the same `value[x]` element remains optional and single-valued, but `Contributor` is not an allowed choice type.

facts.note: The `Contributor` datatype choice is present in the R4 Parameters StructureDefinition and absent from the R6 Parameters StructureDefinition.
FHIR JSON/XML choice-name serializers generated from R6 will not have a `valueContributor` branch for Parameters.
The total count increased because other R6 datatypes were added, but `Contributor` itself was removed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation and serialization break. An R4 `Parameters` instance with `parameter.valueContributor` can satisfy R4 cardinality and `inv-1`, but R6 validators and generated parsers built from the R6 type list have no allowed choice branch for `Contributor`. The risk is high for strict validators and code generators, even though real-world prevalence is likely limited to operations that expose metadata-author/contributor parameters.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The likely impact is failed operation invocation, rejected operation results, or lost contributor metadata rather than direct clinical data corruption.

justification.inferredGoal: Align Parameters value choices with the R6 datatype set after removal of the R4 Contributor datatype.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain a deprecated Contributor choice in base R6 Parameters only if R6 also retained a compatibility Contributor datatype.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The local R6 goal--keeping `Parameters.parameter.value[x]` aligned with the R6 datatype inventory after `Contributor` was removed--is reasonable. A less-breaking base design was possible only by retaining a compatibility `Contributor` datatype and `valueContributor` choice. That would avoid old-valid/new-invalid payloads but would materially undermine cleanup of the R6 datatype set, so the local Parameters break is probably justified while the datatype-level removal remains a separate design question.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best base-design alternative would have been to keep `Contributor` as a deprecated R6 datatype and leave `valueContributor` in `Parameters.parameter.value[x]` for a compatibility cycle. That is more than migration guidance and would preserve R4 Parameters instances that used the branch. The cost is durable legacy surface in validators, schemas, serializers, and generated choice APIs; because `Parameters` is a generic operation carrier, the deprecated branch could remain indefinitely even if most R6 content moved to newer structures. A cross-version extension alone would be a mitigation, not a backward-compatible base R6 design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old valueContributor payloads but keeps an obsolete datatype and choice accessor in a central R6 operation carrier.

evidence.detail: The R4 package defines the `Contributor` datatype; the R6 package file-existence and index checks found no R6 `Contributor` StructureDefinition.

examples.examplesMd: The example is an illustrative R4 fragment showing the removed choice branch. The operation-specific parameter name would be defined by an OperationDefinition.

findings.narrativeMd: `Parameters.parameter.value[x]` lost the `Contributor` choice. This matters because Parameters is the generic wrapper for operation inputs and outputs; many implementations generate a closed set of `value[x]` accessors from the StructureDefinition. A payload using `valueContributor` has no corresponding R6 branch and should be expected to fail strict R6 validation or parsing.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 is old-valid/new-invalid when a parameter uses `valueContributor`. R4 cardinality and `inv-1` allow exactly one value branch, so a `valueContributor` branch can be valid in R4. In R6, the same branch is outside the allowed type domain. This does not create a reverse representability problem because R4 is the version that had the branch.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory operation definitions and test fixtures for `valueContributor`. There is no universal lossless replacement in R6 `Parameters`: `ContactDetail` or `ExtendedContactDetail` may preserve some party/contact information but not necessarily the contributor role; an extension can preserve the exact R4 shape; and operation-specific redesign may be preferable. Tests should include strict validation of migrated Parameters and generated choice accessors.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change was probably tied to removal of the R4 `Contributor` datatype, but the supplied inputs do not show the rationale. A backward-compatible transition could have retained a deprecated `Contributor` branch or supplied a standard cross-version extension. The tradeoff is that R6 would continue carrying an obsolete datatype in a central, normative operation payload resource.

freshReview.narrativeMd: This is a real forward break for the specific choice branch: an R4 operation payload can legally contain `parameter.valueContributor`, while the R6 `Parameters.parameter.value[x]` type list has no `Contributor` branch. Strict R6 validators and generated SDKs will reject or fail to expose that choice. The practical blast radius looks narrow, though: a targeted check of core R4 OperationDefinitions found no operation parameter typed as `Contributor`, and keeping this branch in `Parameters` would require R6 to retain the removed `Contributor` datatype as a compatibility surface. For the local Parameters design, the break is proportionate; any deeper objection belongs mainly to the datatype-level removal.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition-Parameters snapshot element `Parameters.parameter.value[x]` includes type `Contributor`.
R6 StructureDefinition-Parameters snapshot element `Parameters.parameter.value[x]` omits `Contributor`; no R6 `StructureDefinition-Contributor.json` is present.
Targeted search of R4 core `OperationDefinition-*.json` found no `Contributor` parameter type.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 Parameters is FMM 5 and normative, so an old-valid/new-invalid choice removal needs a strong reason. That pressure is mitigated here by the narrow apparent use and by the fact that the local Parameters choice follows the broader R6 datatype inventory.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `valueContributor` instances fall outside the R6 `value[x]` type domain, with related runtime/API/codegen loss of the generated choice accessor.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design would retain a deprecated R6 `Contributor` datatype and keep `valueContributor` for a transition period. That would preserve old payloads, but it is not low cost because it keeps an otherwise removed datatype in validators, schemas, serializers, and generated APIs for a central operation carrier.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing high-impact finding and non-Yes alternative judgment: the hard break is real, but the likely runtime prevalence appears lower than a broad High rating suggests, and the only base alternative has material datatype-level cost.

findings.title: R6 adds six Parameters.parameter.value[x] datatypes with no R4 counterpart

oldState.summary: R4 did not allow `integer64`, `CodeableReference`, `RatioRange`, `Availability`, `ExtendedContactDetail`, or `VirtualServiceDetail` as Parameters value choices.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `Parameters.parameter.value[x]` had no choice names such as `valueInteger64` or `valueCodeableReference`.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 Parameters can carry these new datatypes directly as operation parameter values.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Adding choice types is not an R4-to-R6 validation break: old R4 payloads using the retained choices remain in-domain. It is, however, a high reverse-direction compatibility issue because an R6 Parameters payload may use choice names and datatype shapes that R4 validators, schemas, serializers, and generated classes do not know.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The risk is primarily interoperability failure or lossy conversion of operation parameters. Clinical/business impact depends on the operation using the parameter.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow Parameters to carry the expanded R6 datatype set directly in operation request and response payloads.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not an R4-to-R6 breaking narrowing; this finding is optional type widening that preserves R4-valid value choices.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding R6 datatype choices to the generic Parameters value carrier is justified because it lets R6 operations use the release's datatype set directly. This finding is not itself an old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 break: the newly added choices create reverse-version conversion work, while the separate `Contributor` removal accounts for the R4 choice that no longer carries forward.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible base alternative is applicable for this finding because additive `value[x]` type widening does not invalidate R4 Parameters instances. Encoding these R6-only datatypes through older types or extensions is ordinary R6-to-R4 mitigation, not a less-breaking base R6 design. The only base alternative--not adding the R6 datatype choices--would fail the R6 goal and push avoidable indirection into operation definitions.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 clients need down-conversion rules for R6-only choices, but omitting them would prevent R6 Parameters from carrying R6 datatypes directly.

evidence.detail: The R4 type list lacks all six added R6 datatypes.
The R6 type list includes `integer64`, `CodeableReference`, `RatioRange`, `Availability`, `ExtendedContactDetail`, and `VirtualServiceDetail`.
evidence.quote: integer64, CodeableReference, RatioRange, Availability, ExtendedContactDetail, VirtualServiceDetail

evidence.detail: The R6 XML schema exposes the corresponding serialized choice names including `valueInteger64`, `valueCodeableReference`, `valueRatioRange`, `valueAvailability`, `valueExtendedContactDetail`, and `valueVirtualServiceDetail`.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example is only lossless for a `CodeableReference` that carries `concept` and no `reference`. Other added datatypes need operation-specific mappings or extensions.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 broadens the `Parameters.parameter.value[x]` type domain with six choices that did not exist in R4. This is normal forward evolution, but it is a concrete compatibility issue for cross-version operation gateways and generated models because the serialized choice name itself changes the wire format.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid instances are not invalidated by this widening. The compatibility problem is R6-to-R4: a payload containing `valueCodeableReference`, `valueInteger64`, `valueRatioRange`, `valueAvailability`, `valueExtendedContactDetail`, or `valueVirtualServiceDetail` is outside the R4 Parameters value type list and cannot be represented directly as a legal R4 `value[x]` branch.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For each operation parameter, define an explicit down-conversion rule. Some cases can be mapped with loss under constraints, such as concept-only `CodeableReference` to `CodeableConcept` or reference-only `CodeableReference` to `Reference`. `integer64` may exceed R4 integer limits and may need string/decimal/extension handling. Availability/contact/virtual-service datatypes generally need extensions, resources, or operation redesign for R4 clients.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The widening is probably justified because Parameters should support the release's datatype set. The less-breaking alternative would be to keep the base type list R4-compatible and force new structures through extensions or older types, but that would weaken R6 expressiveness and move complexity into every operation definition.

freshReview.narrativeMd: Adding `integer64`, `CodeableReference`, `RatioRange`, `Availability`, `ExtendedContactDetail`, and `VirtualServiceDetail` is not a forward R4-to-R6 validation break; old R4 `value[x]` choices remain allowed except for the separate `Contributor` removal. It is still a concrete cross-version burden because an R6 operation can now serialize choice names and datatype shapes that an R4 Parameters parser cannot accept. That burden is proportionate: a generic Parameters carrier should be able to carry current R6 datatypes directly, and suppressing the choices would push avoidable work into every operation definition or force extensions/older encodings.
keyEvidence: R4 `Parameters.parameter.value[x]` lacks the six listed R6 datatype choices.
R6 core `OperationDefinition-Subscription-events.json` uses `integer64` parameters, showing at least one added choice is used by core R6 operation surface.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 5/normative status keeps cross-version operation payload stability important, but the change is an additive R6 widening rather than an old-valid/new-invalid R4 break.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 payloads using new choice names such as `valueInteger64` or `valueCodeableReference` cannot be represented directly as valid R4 `Parameters.parameter.value[x]` without operation-specific mapping or loss.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: The base alternative would be to omit these R6 datatype choices or require extensions/older proxy types. That would preserve R4 parser compatibility but would fail the R6 goal of making Parameters a direct carrier for the release's datatype set.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing judgment that this is not an R4-to-R6 hard break and that no useful less-breaking base design exists; the high impact is best understood as reverse-version conversion risk.

findings.title: R6 removes the R4 comment limiting nested Parameters.parameter.part to one level

oldState.summary: R4 `Parameters.parameter.part` had a local comment: `Only one level of nested parameters is allowed.`

semanticText.definition: A named part of a multi-part parameter.
semanticText.comment: Only one level of nested parameters is allowed.

oldState.narrativeMd: The computable R4 content reference was recursive, but the local comment told readers that only one level of nesting was allowed.

newState.summary: R6 keeps the recursive content reference but no longer includes the one-level nesting comment.

semanticText.definition: A named part of a multi-part parameter.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 retains `contentReference: #Parameters.parameter`, allowing nested parts by structure, and the local R4 textual limit is absent.

facts.oldValue: Only one level of nested parameters is allowed.

facts.note: The recursive computable reference did not change.
R6 adds condition metadata pointing to the unchanged `inv-1`; this does not itself add a new validation rule.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a direct StructureDefinition validation break because neither R4 nor R6 adds a FHIRPath invariant limiting nesting depth, and both versions use the same recursive content reference. The risk is semantic and implementation-specific: R4-era systems may have enforced the R4 comment in custom validation, UI builders, or operation handlers, while R6 no longer communicates that limit.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The main risk is failed operation exchange or ambiguous interpretation of deeply nested operation parameters.

justification.inferredGoal: Bring the narrative in line with the recursive Parameters.part content model or allow deeper nested parameter structures.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Replace the one-level comment with transitional clarification about recursive parts and operation-defined nesting limits.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal appears reasonable because the computable content reference is recursive in both versions, while the R4 comment stated a one-level limit without a matching invariant. Removing or revising that inconsistent text is probably justified. A softer text change could have been less disruptive, but it would only partially preserve compatibility if R6 operations actually rely on multiple nesting levels.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base text design would have replaced the R4 sentence with explicit guidance such as allowing deeper nesting only when defined by the operation and warning that some R4 implementations may enforce a one-level convention. That would be a real base-definition alternative, not conversion tooling. It is only partial because the old assumption cannot be fully preserved while also allowing arbitrarily nested R6 parameter parts; keeping transitional language could also perpetuate uncertainty about whether the recursive model is normative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Clarification would reduce surprise for R4-era implementers, but cannot make old one-level processors accept genuinely deeper R6 structures and may preserve ambiguity.

evidence.detail: R4 includes a local comment limiting nested parameters to one level.
evidence.quote: Only one level of nested parameters is allowed.

evidence.detail: R6 has no equivalent comment and keeps `contentReference` to `#Parameters.parameter`.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment is structurally representable by the R4 content reference, but it conflicts with the R4 comment if an implementation treats that comment as a conformance rule.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 removes the explicit R4 statement that only one level of nested `part` is allowed. Because `part` recursively references `Parameters.parameter`, implementations may have differed: some followed the recursive model, while others enforced the text. R6 tilts the definition toward recursive use by omitting the textual limit.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A standards validator that only evaluates the listed FHIRPath constraints is unlikely to reject deeper nesting in either version. The break is therefore not hard instance-breaking in the computable StructureDefinition. It is a compatibility risk for systems that implemented the R4 comment as an extra rule and then receive R6 Parameters with more than one nested `part` level.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When bridging R6 to R4, check whether the target R4 system has a custom nesting-depth limit. If it does, flattening or operation-specific restructuring may be required, and the transform may be lossy because nested grouping can carry meaning. Test operation handlers with zero, one, and multiple part nesting levels.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Removing an unenforced comment may be justified if the real model has always been recursive. A backward-compatible alternative would have added explicit clarification rather than deleting the limit outright, but without narrative change notes the intended semantics remain a human-review point.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm against the rendered R6 Parameters page or ballot notes whether deeper nesting is explicitly intended, merely tolerated, or still discouraged elsewhere.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The computable model did not become stricter. R4 and R6 both use `contentReference: #Parameters.parameter` for `parameter.part`, and neither version has a FHIRPath invariant limiting nesting depth. R6 removed a prose sentence that conflicted with the recursive structure and with evidence from core R4 OperationDefinitions that already define nested parameter parts. A custom R4 implementation that enforced the old sentence could still need policy work, but that is not a base R4-to-R6 break caused by R6.
keyEvidence: R4 `Parameters.parameter.part` has comment `Only one level of nested parameters is allowed.`
R4 and R6 both retain `contentReference: #Parameters.parameter`; no depth-limiting FHIRPath constraint was added or removed.
Targeted checks found R4 core OperationDefinitions with nested `part` depth greater than one, including CodeSystem and ConceptMap operations.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 5/normative status argues for caution with conformance text, but here the R6 change removes an inconsistent non-computable statement rather than invalidating conformant instances.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: the only change is removal of prose; structural validation remains recursive and unchanged for this path.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have replaced the sentence with transitional clarification about recursive parts and operation-defined limits. That might help readers, but it is not needed to preserve R4-valid instances and would risk perpetuating the old inconsistency.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with the existing Medium impact and partial alternative framing: the evidence points to a documentation cleanup with no meaningful path-level compatibility problem.

findings.title: R6 text explicitly allows additional resources in Parameters.parameter.resource

oldState.summary: R4 `parameter.resource` was typed as `Resource` with no local mention of additional resources.

semanticText.definition: If the parameter is a whole resource.
semanticText.comment: When resolving references in resources, the operation definition may specify how references may be resolved between parameters. If a reference cannot be resolved between the parameters, the application should fall back to it's general resource resolution methods.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed a whole `Resource` parameter but did not locally call out additional/custom resource definitions.

newState.summary: R6 keeps type `Resource` but adds local text that the resource may be a FHIR-defined resource or an additional resource.

semanticText.definition: Conveys the content if the parameter is a whole resource.
semanticText.comment: This may be a resource defined in the FHIR specification, or an [additional resource](resource.html#additional). When resolving references in resources, the operation definition may specify how references may be resolved between parameters. If a reference cannot be resolved between the parameters, the application should fall back to its general resource resolution methods.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 explicitly widens the expected kinds of resource payloads that may appear in `Parameters.parameter.resource`.

facts.note: The formal type did not change.

facts.oldValue: No local mention of additional resources.
facts.newValue: This may be a resource defined in the FHIR specification, or an [additional resource](resource.html#additional).

impact.impactRationaleMd: The formal type remains `Resource`, so ordinary R4 resource parameters are not invalidated. The compatibility risk is in R6-to-R4 exchange: if an R6 Parameters payload carries an additional resource whose `resourceType` is not known to R4 core models, strict R4 parsers and validators may reject it or require an out-of-band StructureDefinition.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The main impact is operation interoperability and parser failure. Business impact depends on whether the operation uses additional resources for essential content.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify that Parameters can transport both specification-defined resources and R6 additional resources as whole-resource operation parameters.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not an R4-to-R6 instance-breaking local design change; the formal type remains Resource and ordinary R4 resource parameters remain valid.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The local change is a semantic clarification that `parameter.resource` may carry R6 additional resources while keeping the same `Resource` type and cardinality. Because it does not invalidate ordinary R4 Parameters instances, the compatibility issue is mainly reverse-version parsing of resource types unknown to R4. The broader additional-resource design belongs to the Resource infrastructure analysis, so this local Parameters text is probably justified rather than an avoidable R4-to-R6 base break.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible alternative is applicable in the R4-to-R6 sense. Requiring profiles or implementation guides to opt into additional resources would be a stricter design with some R4 interoperability benefits, but it would not meet the same base R6 goal of documenting `Parameters` as a generic carrier for both specification-defined and additional resources. For R4 systems, profiles, rejection policies, Binary wrapping, extensions, or out-of-band definitions are migration mitigations rather than base R6 alternatives.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 parsers may need policies for R6 additional resources, but suppressing the base text would undercut R6's generic resource transport goal.

evidence.detail: R4 discusses reference resolution between parameters but does not mention additional resources.
R6 says the resource may be a FHIR specification resource or an additional resource.
evidence.quote: This may be a resource defined in the FHIR specification, or an [additional resource](resource.html#additional).

examples.examplesMd: No concrete additional-resource instance was validated from the supplied package. The risk applies when an R6 operation uses `parameter.resource` with a resource definition unavailable to an R4 core parser.

findings.narrativeMd: `Parameters.parameter.resource` is still formally typed as `Resource`, but R6 explicitly documents that the payload may be an additional resource. That can surprise R4-era implementations that treat whole-resource parameters as one of the fixed R4 core resource classes.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: There is no R4-to-R6 hard validation break for ordinary resource parameters. The R6-to-R4 problem arises when the nested resource's concrete `resourceType` is outside the R4 core package. Such a payload may require an extra StructureDefinition or may be impossible for a closed generated R4 model to parse.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For cross-version operation gateways, detect the concrete `resourceType` under `parameter.resource`. If it is not an R4 core resource, decide whether the operation can transform it to an R4 resource, carry it through Binary/extension/out-of-band packaging, or reject it with a clear OperationOutcome. Include parser tests with unknown resourceType values if additional resources are in scope.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change may be justified by R6's broader resource model, but the base `Resource`/additional-resource analysis belongs with the `Resource` infrastructure report. A backward-compatible local alternative would have required operation definitions or profiles to opt into additional resources instead of placing the allowance in the base Parameters text.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Review the R6 additional-resource narrative and any operation definitions that use additional resources before assigning a final prevalence or safety rating.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `Parameters.parameter.resource` remains typed as `Resource` with the same cardinality and invariant relationship. R6 adds prose saying the contained resource may be a specification-defined resource or an additional resource. That can matter to an R4-only parser receiving an R6 payload with an unknown concrete `resourceType`, but that is a reverse-version/general additional-resource issue rather than a local R4-to-R6 break in Parameters. Ordinary R4 resource-valued parameters are not made invalid.
keyEvidence: R4 and R6 both define `Parameters.parameter.resource` as type `Resource` with cardinality `0..1`.
R6 adds the comment phrase `This may be a resource defined in the FHIR specification, or an additional resource`.
The unchanged `inv-1` relationship still controls the choice between `value[x]`, `resource`, and `part`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Normative FMM 5 status raises sensitivity to semantic shifts, but the formal path shape is unchanged and the risk is reverse-only for R4 systems that cannot handle R6 additional resources.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: R6 clarifies allowed resource kinds in prose; any R6-to-R4 parser failure comes from unknown concrete resources rather than a narrowed Parameters element.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A stricter base design could require operation definitions or profiles to opt into additional resources. That would be more restrictive and somewhat friendlier to closed R4 parsers, but it would not meet the R6 goal of documenting Parameters as a generic whole-resource operation carrier.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with the existing Medium/High reverse-risk framing for this local finding: the concern is real for cross-version additional-resource handling, but the Parameters path itself has no meaningful R4-to-R6 compatibility problem.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, base definition, derivation, abstract flag, and active status are stable.
The local element paths `Parameters.parameter`, `.name`, `.value[x]`, `.resource`, and `.part` remain present with the same identities. Type-choice changes are covered separately.

The local `inv-1` FHIRPath expression remains `(part.exists() and value.empty() and resource.empty()) or (part.empty() and (value.exists() xor resource.exists()))`. R6 adds condition metadata on `part`, but no new local validation expression.
`Parameters.parameter.resource` remains type `Resource` with no target profile list. The R6 additional-resource text is handled as a semantic finding, not a formal reference-target delta.
No locally defined Parameters elements have terminology bindings. The inherited `Resource.language` binding change is out of scope.
No local fixed value, pattern, or default value constraints were found on Parameters-specific elements.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex limit changes were found on Parameters-specific elements.
Local `parameter`, `name`, `value[x]`, `resource`, and `part` modifier flags remain false or absent. Inherited modifier-extension behavior is out of scope.
The local Parameters-specific elements remain summary elements where expected; no local summary flag changed materially.
No local slicing was added, removed, or changed for Parameters-specific elements.

Material serialization impact is limited to the `value[x]` choice-name set and is covered in findings. The R6 XML schema confirms the new choice element names; the local R4 package did not include an R4 Parameters XML schema for direct schema-to-schema comparison.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Root description broadens wording from operation-only/no endpoint to REST or messaging operation context
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The formal resource identity, base type, elements, and constraints do not change. Existing R4 operation Parameters remain structurally valid in R6 unless they use a removed choice type.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Operation frameworks should note the R6 wording that includes operations invoked directly from REST or within messaging and says Parameters is not persisted or referenced by other resources. This may affect documentation and policy checks more than instance validation.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 marks part as conditioned by unchanged inv-1
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The condition annotation points to the same `inv-1` rule already present on `Parameters.parameter`; it does not change cardinality or add a new FHIRPath expression.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tools that use ElementDefinition.condition for UI hints may newly show `part` as related to `inv-1`, but validation behavior should be the same.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 explicitly records mustSupport false on local elements
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 generally omitted `mustSupport` where false; R6 explicitly records false. This does not require implementations to support new elements.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Diff tools should normalize absent and explicit false `mustSupport` values to avoid false positives.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: value[x] and resource definitions were reworded to say they convey content
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The rewording clarifies the purpose of the elements but does not alter their cardinality, name, or invariant relationship.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Documentation generators may show changed text, but validation behavior is governed by the type-domain findings and unchanged `inv-1`.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Inherited Resource changes, including `language`, `id`, `implicitRules`, and the broader additional-resource infrastructure, are intentionally excluded from local Parameters findings but affect complete migration planning.
`Contributor` removal is the underlying cause of the local `valueContributor` break. A datatype-level report should define the preferred R6 migration target and lossless/lossy transform options.

followUpDependencies.nameOrUrl: integer64, CodeableReference, RatioRange, Availability, ExtendedContactDetail, VirtualServiceDetail
followUpDependencies.reasonMd: These R6 datatypes are local `Parameters.value[x]` additions but their internal R4 compatibility, value limits, and safe down-conversions belong to their datatype reports.
Actual migration impact depends on which operation definitions declare Parameters that use the removed or added datatypes, nested parts, or additional resource payloads.
